Living in Washington has many benefits — access to nature despite being in a big city, countless job opportunities, and entertainment and culture always just around the corner. As a homeowner in the state, life is almost ideal. But there is one challenge that can make life a little tricky… Washington’s diverse climate and geography.

blocks.text: All About Deck Staining

Now, let’s round back to the deck staining vs deck painting discourse, starting with the former. Deck staining involves applying a specially formulated stain to your decking materials, penetrating the surface. Transparent stains let the natural wood grain show, while semi-transparent and solid stains offer more color and coverage.
blocks.html: Now, let’s round back to the deck staining vs deck painting discourse, starting with the former. Deck staining involves applying a specially formulated stain to your decking materials, penetrating the surface. Transparent stains let the natural wood grain show, while semi-transparent and solid stains offer more color and coverage.

blocks.text: Stains form a protective barrier that prevents water from soaking into the materials, avoiding swelling, warping, and rotting. Some also have mildew-resistant properties for more moisture-related issues.

blocks.text: Staining also involves UV-blocking agents that safeguard materials from sun damage and does not typically result in peeling or cracking as paint can.

Deck staining comes with several advantages, including the following:

blocks.text: Easy to Apply: Stain typically goes on smoothly, not requiring much precision. It is less likely to drip or streak, making it an exciting choice for DIY enthusiasts.

blocks.text: Highlights Wood’s Natural Beauty: Staining preserves and highlights the beauty of the wood, from cedar and redwood to teak.

blocks.text: The Cons
There are drawbacks to consider before staining, such as the following:

blocks.text: Fading Fast in Sunlight: UV rays eventually break down the stain, causing it to lose its vibrant color and finish.

blocks.text: Requires Reapplication: Wear and tear can degrade stains faster than paint, so more frequent reapplication may be necessary.

blocks.text: The Power of Deck Painting

Moving on to the latter part of the deck staining vs deck painting battle, Washington homeowners have even more factors to think about. Deck painting involves applying a layer of paint to the surface of your deck, creating a solid, opaque finish that completely covers it. You can go for oil-based, acrylic, latex, or epoxy paint, based on the level of maintenance you are willing to carry out.

blocks.text: Unlike stains, which go through the decking material, paint sits on top. As such, your deck gets a more robust shield against rot, discoloration, and wear. Paint can also help prevent splinters, with a smooth, even surface for walking and furniture placement.
